reasoning: A hybrid strategy is chosen because autonomous reasoning can efficiently identify initial patterns in shared features across misclassified instances, while XAI tools provide quantitative, model-agnostic feature attributions to validate and strengthen the hypothesis of spurious correlations. This combination allows for both qualitative insight and robust statistical validation of shared feature influence.

autonomous_tasks.query: List all features that appear in every misclassified instance (13590, 2021, 41382) and identify if any feature has a semantically inconsistent or redundant value across them.
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A list of features that are common across all three instances, along with notes on any semantically questionable or redundant values

autonomous_tasks.query: Why might a feature that is not semantically related to income (e.g., marital status, workclass) have high predictive power in this model despite not being directly relevant to the target variable?
autonomous_tasks.expected_output: A hypothesis about spurious correlation, such as a feature being correlated with class labels due to data distribution or historical biases

tool_selection.reasoning: SHAP provides consistent, interpretable attribution scores across instances and identifies features with high influence in misclassified cases. LIME and Integrated Gradients offer local and global sensitivity, helping to confirm if high attribution is consistent and not due to noise. Sensitivity analysis isolates the causal effect of each feature by ablation, verifying whether removing a feature changes predictions significantly — a key test for spuriousness.
